headline: Genome-language models and curated databases advance viral sequence detection
label: Viral Sequence Detection Methods
summary: Genome-language models are now benchmarked against BLAST, while metagenomic viral profilers and compressed protein indexes expand detection scale.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational detection of viral sequences in genomes and metagenomes, pairing curated references with learned models or refined profiling. CheckAMG combines curated annotation scoring with a finetuned genome-language model to identify viral auxiliary genes. A benchmark of genomic foundation models, Nucleotide Transformer and DNABERT, against BLAST on RVDB reports NTv3-650M at 0.93 relative to BLAST. EsViritu pairs iterative greedy clustering and LCA refinement with a curated virus database for metagenomic detection and genome recovery. Centrifuger's run-block compressed FM-index for protein databases cuts memory over a third relative to Kaiju. ProBord maps proviral borders at single-base resolution, yielding a 430,134-provirus database. What is new is genome-language models entering annotation pipelines alongside compact, searchable reference resources.
